files.why: Dedicated status badge mirroring billing's InvoiceStatusBadge.vue — encapsulates the AppointmentStatus→Badge-variant colour lookup so the day view matches how invoices present status.
Replace the inline <Badge> + local VARIANT_BY_STATUS map with the new AppointmentStatusBadge component so the day view (which renders this card) shows the status the same way invoices do.

uncertain: Whether a new AppointmentStatusBadge component is even wanted: AppointmentCard.vue already renders a coloured, variant-mapped status Badge, so extracting one is an architectural-consistency refactor (parallel to InvoiceStatusBadge), not net-new UI. Under README rule 7 a single same-reason usage would normally be left inline/duplicated, so this extraction is arguably premature.

Whether the badge should be rendered directly in DayView.vue rather than inside AppointmentCard.vue — DayView delegates each appointment to AppointmentCard, so I placed it in the card, but 'in the day view' could be read as the view itself.

Whether the invoice parity is meant to include a derived/override state (InvoiceStatusBadge has an `overdue` override) — appointments have no analogous derived status today, so I assumed a plain status→variant mapping.
questions: The day view already shows a coloured appointment status label (AppointmentCard.vue renders a Badge with scheduled=default, completed=success, cancelled=outline). Was this ticket filed against an older state, or is the real ask to refactor it into a dedicated AppointmentStatusBadge component for consistency with InvoiceStatusBadge?
Should appointment statuses reuse the exact same colour semantics as invoices (e.g. success=green for completed/paid, outline for cancelled/void), or is a scheduling-specific colour mapping expected?
Is there any derived state to surface (e.g. a 'conflict' or 'past-due'/'no-show' style override, mirroring the invoice 'overdue' override), or strictly the three literal AppointmentStatus values?
